Hilario: This pertains to your letters dated 10 October 2017 and 18 July 2018 requesting this Department's legal opinion on this query: "As Acting VIZe Mayor, will Hon. Maria Nancy M. Socrates acquired thepower to appoint, suspend, dismiss or discipline employees akin to an Acting Local Chief Executive under the conditions set forth under Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991?" Before we answer your query, it is important to know the difference between the terms "Acting" and "Officer-in-charge'! Relative thereto, the Civil Service Commission said that: "(I)t must be noted that a designation under acting capacity may be differentiated from a designation as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) in such a manner that an OIC enjoys limited powers which are confined to functions of administration and ensuring that the office continues its usual activities. The OIC may not be deemed to possess the power to appoint employees as the same involves the exercise of discretion which is beyond the power dan OIC On the other hand, as aptly ruled by the Commission in the case of Amado S. Day, ci entails not onl fun • ns attached to n also the exercise of discretion. This considering that Che person designated is deemed te the bent e •ti 1" In the herein situation, Hon. Nancy Socrates is the Acting Vice Mayor in the City of Puerto Princesa. Palawan. Based on the above definition of the term "Acting", she should be treated the same as "incumbent in the position". It follows, therefore, that she can perform all the duties and powers of the Office of the Vice Mayor provided under Section 456 of the Local Government Code (LGC). Included therein is this provision: CSC Resolution No 000778, 24 March 2000 Page I of 2

"Subject to civil service law, rules and regulations, appoint all officials and employees of the sangguniang panlungsod, except those whose manner of appointment is specifically provided in the Code. " However, this provision of law is subject also to the same rule under Section 46 (a) of the LGC where the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. This is to prevent unfairness in a situation wherein the Acting Mayor cannot do such acts while the Acting Vice Mayor can perform the same even if the temporary incapacity does not exceed 30 working days. In addition, this Department in its Legal Opinion No. 49 S. 2018, opined that "On the other hand, the highest ranking SP member, as we rtainin t th f the ministeri us tion attached t the well a the e discretion. However, the Presiding Officership function is not automatically given to him in Vléw if the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case ofGamboa vs. Aguirre2stating that the issue of Presiding Officership in this kind of situation shall be resolved applying Section 49(b) of the LGC, in which case, the majority of those present members there being a quorum shall elect from among themselves the temporary Presiding Officer for that session. " In view herein, please note that Presiding Officership is not automatic in this case but subject to the provision of Section 49 (b) of the LGC. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: C. SACENDONCILLO Assistant Secretary Copy furnished: Dir. Florida M.
